scenario: I volunteer at a winter emergency shelter that becomes overcrowded whenever temperatures drop, and because beds are limited, the shelter prioritizes people with serious medical or physical vulnerabilities. On one especially busy night, I was helping sort intake forms while staff tried to place the last available beds. The temperature outside is very cold, so anyone who is unable to be placed with a bed will suffer outside. A man approached my coworker and pointed out several severe medical conditions he had listed, which would move him to the top of the priority list. Later, I overheard him telling a friend that he had lied about those conditions to nab a spot inside. There are still a handful of people more vulnerable than the man waiting to have their intake forms processed. If I cross out information on the man’s intake form, his bed will go to someone more vulnerable. If I do not do this, a more vulnerable person will be turned away and left to suffer in the cold.
entities: 1 volunteer narrator,1 coworker,1 man who lied about severe medical conditions to get a bed,1 friend the man spoke to,1+ other more vulnerable shelter seekers still waiting to have their intake forms processed,1+ other shelter staff members trying to place the last available beds,I
outcomes: The man keeps his high-priority placement for a bed.
The man stays inside the shelter instead of outside in the cold.
Shelter staff continue relying on false medical information about the man.
A more vulnerable person loses access to the last available bed.
A more vulnerable person is turned away from the shelter.
A more vulnerable person suffers outside in the cold.
I experience distress about allowing a more vulnerable person to be left outside.
